features.name: any_oc_link_gov_edu_org
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain a link to a .gov, .edu, or .org website?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as JSON list of strings; malformed/missing -> null; empty list -> 0. For each comment, find URLs via regex r'https?://[^\s)\]>]+|www\.[^\s)\]>]+'; extract host (text after scheme up to first '/', '?', '#' or ':'), lowercase; a URL matches if host ends with '.gov', '.edu' or '.org' (also e.g. .gov.uk/.edu.au where gov/edu is a dot-delimited label ending the TLD segment). Return 1 if any comment has a matching URL, else 0.

h0: any_oc_link_gov_edu_org has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
h1: Discussions with a counter-argument linking to .gov, .edu or .org sites are more likely to have the OP change their view.
note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the delta outcome (OP view change) at row level. Raw URL text matching is mechanical; comments may contain outcome announcements and URL timing relative to the outcome is unknown. The hypothesis has no explicit comparison group; the implied comparison is rows with no such link (including rows with only other-domain links). Links to .org sites include any organization, e.g. wikipedia.org. Link presence does not imply the comment's claim is supported by the link. Association only.
